claims.text: The as-cast MnNiSi-based alloy has a continuous matrix exhibiting a first-order magneto-structural transition.
Aging at 520°C for 2–4 hours followed by controlled cooling will induce nano-scale MnSi precipitates in the MnNiSi-based alloy.
The induced MnSi precipitates will be uniformly dispersed within the parent matrix.
An inert atmosphere will prevent oxidation during the aging treatment.
Precise control of aging temperature and time will promote nano-scale MnSi precipitation without excessive coarsening.
Nano-scale MnSi precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by the precipitates will increase yield strength through precipitation strengthening.
Precipitation strengthening by nano-scale MnSi precipitates will increase toughness.
The matrix will largely preserve the magneto-structural transition after aging and precipitation.
Preservation of the magneto-structural transition will retain a large magnetocaloric effect.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the aged alloy will have higher yield strength.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the aged alloy will have improved toughness.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the aged alloy will retain its magnetocaloric effect with no more than a minimal reduction.
The as-cast baseline has inferior mechanical properties relative to the proposed heat-treated alloy.
The beneficial combination of mechanical and magnetocaloric properties depends on the precipitates remaining nano-scale.
Precipitate coarsening may alter phase-transformation kinetics or broaden the magnetic transition.
Larger precipitates produced by deviations in aging temperature or time may compromise magnetocaloric properties.
